MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 8, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:01 p.m., on October 8, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 5, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  Council Member Sachs

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiator, Government Code Section 54956.8. The
  Property Commonly Referred to as "Casta del Sol Golf Course" located at 27601
  Casta del Sol, Mission Viejo, California. City of Mission Viejo Negotiators: City
  Manager Dennis Wilbert, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith
  Rattay, Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas and City Attorney William
  Curley, III. Negotiating Party: American Golf Corporation Mr. J. Hinckley,
  President and Mr. Foley, General Counsel Under Discussion Price and Terms.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: Two
  (2) potential cases.

City Council Minutes  1  October 8, 2019
 CS3. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project
  v. The City of Mission Viejo.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m. Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with four Council Members present and one absent.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council considered two Closed Session items with
three topics. The Council received updates and gave direction to staff but no reportable actions
occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Annual Walk Against Drugs

  Received presentation from Crime Prevention Specialist Khatra Molina.

P2. Featured Business of the Month - iFinance Mortgage, Inc.

  Presented proclamation to John Rodriguez of iFinance Mortgage, Inc.

P3. Proclaim October 6 through 12, 2019 To Be "Fire Prevention Week"

  Presented proclamation to Fire Chief Rob Capobianco.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Michelle Claud-Clemente, Mission Viejo Animal Services Manager: Invited the City Council to
the 25th Annual DAWG Walk and Pet Fair which will take place on Sunday October 13, starting
at 9:00 a.m.

Michael Rochter, M.V.: Stated that he believes that climate change is real and he addressed some
misconceptions on the topic. He recommended the book “Beyond Debate: The 50 misconception
of Climate Change,” by University of California, Irvine Professor Shahir Masri.

Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: Voiced his concern with people texting while driving and suggested the City
employ more deputies for enforcement.

Terry Yapp, M.V.: Expressed his concern with drug detox facilities within residential
neighborhoods throughout the City. He encouraged the City to lobby the Governor of California,

City Council Minutes  2  October 8, 2019
 State Legislators, and local Representatives.

Christine Saracino, M.V.: Stated that she is very concerned for the young children in her
neighborhood because of a new sober living and drug detox home.

Naik Khairzada, Mission Viejo Community of Character Committee Member, M.V.: Announced
that the character word for the month of October is respect.

Maureen Maloof, M.V.: Discussed her nonprofit “Uniforms for Hope” which raises money to buy
school uniforms for needy children overseas. Those interested in volunteering may contract her
through www.uniformsforhope.org and she announced that there will be a fundraiser on Saturday,
November 16 from 2:00 to 3:00 p.m. at the Sway Ballroom in Laguna Hills.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: Stated that she is not in favor of the City purchasing the Casta del Sol golf
course. She expressed concerns about the property being in a flood zone and the huge liability it
will bring to the City.

Randy Johnson, R.S.M.: Spoke about his locksmith business and touched upon the different type
of safes that residents can have in their home to protect property from fire and theft.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Sachs

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 24, 2019, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated September 13, 2019 in the Amount of $1,400,401.10

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated September 20, 2019 in the Amount of $375,814.25

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Fiscal Year End June 30,
  2019

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  October 8, 2019
 5.  Tyler Munis ERP Financial, HR, and Payroll Software Renewal

  Approved purchase order to Tyler Technologies, Inc. for 1-year renewal term of software
  licensing and support for Munis ERP Financial, Human Resources, and Payroll system in the
  amount of $64,810.11.

6.  Library Automated System Software and Hardware Support Agreement

  Approved issuance of a purchase order for 1-year in the amount of $71,929.30 for
  maintenance and support of the Library Automated Systems (ALS) Software and Hardware
  Agreement with SirsiDynix, Inc.

7.  Parking Restrictions on Public Streets

  Adopted Ordinance 19-331 Amending Chapter 12.08.010 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code Regarding Parking Restrictions on Public Streets.

8.  Craycraft Park Restroom Building (CIP 315)

  Awarded contract to Public Restroom Company for the purchase, delivery and installation of
  a Prefabricated Restroom Building at Craycraft Park in an amount not to exceed $471,369.00.

9.  Landscape and Irrigation Supplies - SiteOne Landscape Supply

  Approved Change Order to the existing Purchase Order for SiteOne Landscape Supply for
  the subject services in an amount not to exceed $60,000.00.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

10. Purchase of Casta Del Sol Public Golf Property for the Purpose of Preserving the Golf
  Course and Open Space

  Mayor Raths announced that this item will be continued to Monday, October 14, 2019, at
  6:00 p.m. so that Council Member Sachs will be in attendance to vote on the matter. He noted
  that due to the Jewish Holiday Yom Kippur, Council Member Sachs was unable to attend
  this evening and the Council felt it was pertinent that all five members be in attendance for
  this decision.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg gave the staff report.

  Ingmar Forster, M.V.: Spoke in opposition to the purchase of the golf course, expressing
  concern for the immediate and future costs to the City and taxpayers. He stated that he is in
  favor of the golf course either remaining a golf course or open space.

  Joyce Elia, M.V.: Stated she is not in favor and has concerns about the City’s reserves. She
  asked the Council to rethink the purchase of the golf course.

City Council Minutes  4  October 8, 2019
   Rolland Graham, M.V.: Spoke in favor of the purchase of the golf course and considered the
  purchase of the land to be an asset to the City.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Discussed the failure of Measure D from the 2010 Election. She
  expressed concerns with the future costs if the City purchases the golf course.

  Suzanne Harder, M.V.: Spoke in favor of the purchase of the golf course and agreed with the
  City Attorney’s statement that ownership of a property is the way to have control. She
  discussed needed maintenance and suggested that the bar and restaurant remain open longer.

  Rick Sandzimier, M.V. Commended the leadership of the City and spoke in favor of the
  purchase of the golf course. He stated that he trusts the City Council in their decision-making.

11. City of Mission Viejo Comprehensive Bikeway and Transportation Connectivity
  Master Plan

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The City Council praised Assistant City Manager Rattay for all of his hard work on this
  project.

  By consensus the Council received the Comprehensive Bikeway and Transportation
  Connectivity Master Plan.

NEW BUSINESS

12. Proposed Ordinance Adopting the 2019 California Building and Fire Codes, the
  International Swimming Pool and Spa Code and the International Property
  Maintenance Code.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to (1)
  introduce Ordinance 19-332 Adopting by Reference the 2019 Editions of the California
  Building, Residential, Plumbing, Electrical, Mechanical, Green Building Standards,
  Historical Building, and Existing Building Codes, and the 2018 Editions of the International
  Swimming Pool and Spa Code and International Property Maintenance Code, Together, with
  Certain Appendices and Amendments Thereto, and Amending Title 8 of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code; (2) introduce Ordinance 19-333 Adopting by Reference the 2019
  California Fire Code, Together with Certain Amendments and Deletions; and (3) schedule a
  Public Hearing for November 12, 2019 to Adopt the Ordinances Identified in Items (1) and
  (2).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs
City Council Minutes  5  October 8, 2019
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  No report given.

14.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received reports from Mayor Raths, Council Member Kelley, and Council Member
  Bucknum.

STAFF REPORTS

15. CalPERS Pension Plan Actuarial Valuation Report for June 30, 2018

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  By consensus the City Council received and filed the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

16. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she attended the Nadadores Annual Fall Foundation
Benefit that raises funds to help pay back the money owed for the Aquatics Center improvements.
She also outlined her attendance at “Walk to School” at Bathgate Elementary and she thanked the
school for a great event. Council Member Bucknum reminded residents of the upcoming annual
Walk Against Drugs and the annual DAWG Walk. She announced that she is going to try some
of the bike trails that Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay referenced in his staff report this
evening.

Council Member Kelley

Announced that she attended the same events as Council Member Bucknum and she encouraged
residents to attend the DAWG Walk this coming Sunday and the Drug Abuse Expo on Wednesday,
October 16 at the Norman P. Murray Center from 6:00 p.m.to 8:00 p.m. She stated that there will
be three speakers; Dr. Michael Ritter from Mission Hospital who will speak about the dangers and
impacts of drug abuse, Community Resource Officer Deputy Hume who will speak on current and
emerging drug trends and lastly a representative from Orange County Health Care Agency will
talk about youth resiliency for drug resistance and tips on fortifying young people to say no to
drugs. She stated that there will be approximately ten organizations that will provide information
to attendees. Council Member Kelley encouraged people to register online on the City’s website
or email her directly. She also reminded residents that the annual Drug Walk is October 19 starting
City Council Minutes  6  October 8, 2019
 at Mission Viejo High School. She asked City staff to come back at some point to report on the
nuances of drug detox homes versus sober living homes. Council Member Kelley announced that
the Community of Character word for the month of October is respect and the character movie,
Remember the Titans, will be playing in the Council Chamber on Sunday, October 13 at 2:00 p.m.
She thanked Naik Khairzada for speaking tonight on the character word of the month and said he
did an excellent job.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that he had a great time attending the Nadadores event at the
Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club and that a lot of money was raised for their program as well as to pay
their obligation back to the City. He reported that earlier in the evening Keith Rattay mentioned
that work has begun at lower Curtis Park and on the widening of the freeway onramp at La Paz
Road. He explained that the two projects are connected because clean dirt from the freeway
widening is being placed behind Curtis Park to create more sports fields and there is substantial
cost savings to the City because of this. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that he will be
attending the Marine Adoption Committee’s “Tee it Up for Marines” golf tournament this
upcoming Friday. He also mentioned how much his dogs have enjoyed the DAWG Walk and he
shared his plans to attend the event again this year. Lastly, he stated that he is excited to vote on
the purchase of the Casta del Sol Golf Course next Monday and looks forward to hearing input
from residents.

Mayor Raths

17. Former Mission Viejo Mayor’s Dinner

  The Mayor announced that he has plans to host a former Mayor’s dinner on December 7,
  2019, from 5:00 – 8:00 p.m. at a home on Lake Mission Viejo. He thanked Renata Winter
  for her help in providing addresses for the former Mayors.

Mayor Raths reported that he attended Capo Valley High School’s College Fair last night and had
a great time.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:36 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Monday October 14, 2019, at 6:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 22, 2019

City Council Minutes  7  October 8, 2019
